newsitem.title: JAPAN: New bonds to be well absorbed by Japan investors.
newsitem.headline: New bonds to be well absorbed by Japan investors.

text.p: Newly launched samurai bonds and Eurobonds issued by foreign corporations and governments are expected to be well-absorbed by Japanese corporations and private investors, underwriting sources said on Thursday.

The World Bank's $1 billion worth of 5.68 percent three-year Eurobonds have been well-received by Japanese investors since the beginning of the subscription on Wednesday, said an underwriter at Yamaichi Securities, lead manager for the issue. The subscription ends on September 24.
"We can already see favourable demand by domestic investors a day after the subscription date," the underwriter said.
Other issues, which were launched on Wednesday, are also expected to attract buying interest from Japanese corporations, but mostly from private investors, underwriters said.
Mexico launched 70 billion yen worth of 5.0 percent five-year samurai bonds priced at par.
"A coupon of five percent should be quite attractive despite a low credit rating," one underwriter said. "This Mexican issue should attract interest both from corporate and private investors."
Moody's Investors Service said on Thursday that it had assigned its Ba2 rating to Mexico's samurai bonds.

Underwriters said the market would see more low rated bonds issued in the near future. These bond issues increased after the Finance Ministry's wide-ranging deregulation measures in January, which allowed foreign issuers with lower ratings to issue the bonds.
Shortly after the deregulation, overseas issuers with low credit ratings actively issued bonds in Japan.
A series of issues from such borrowers as Mexico, Brazil and Turkey took place in the spring.
Underwriters said the government of Romania has also been been considering launching samurai bonds here.

Private investors' appetite for samurai bonds should remain strong. The investors, who are reluctant to buy domestic instruments due to low interest rates, have raised their foreign bond holdings to about three trillion yen in the past year, underwriters said.
On the corporate side, International Business Machines Corp (IBM) on Wednesday launched 50 billion yen worth of 5.3 percent three-year yen/dollar dual-currency samurai bonds.
"I don't see much problem for IBM's samurais to get absorbed. It should be sold rather quickly," a third underwriter said.
